---
title: "Regrid a challenger onto the GLO12 grid"
---

OceanBench scores challengers on regular latitude-longitude grids at 1, 1/4 or 1/12 degree.
A model on another grid (curvilinear, rotated, or regular at another spacing) must first be brought onto one of them.
The `oceanbench.helpers.challengers` module does this for CROCO output: one call turns a CROCO history file into a challenger dataset on the GLO12 1/12 degree grid and its 50 depth levels, ready to be scored against GLO12.

## Installation

The regridding needs [pyresample](https://pyresample.readthedocs.io), which is an optional dependency:

``` bash
pip install "oceanbench[regridding]"
```

## Usage

``` python
import oceanbench
from oceanbench.helpers import challengers

challenger = challengers.croco_to_glo12_challenger("croco_his.nc")
challenger.to_netcdf("croco_challenger.nc")

agulhas = oceanbench.regions.custom(
    identifier="agulhas",
    display_name="Agulhas",
    minimum_latitude=-39.0,
    maximum_latitude=-33.0,
    minimum_longitude=18.0,
    maximum_longitude=29.0,
)
oceanbench.metrics.rmsd_of_variables_compared_to_glo12_analysis(challenger, region=agulhas)
```

The region should leave out the sponge layer along the open boundaries of a regional model, where the damped small-scale variability would otherwise enter the scores.
In the Agulhas example above, it leaves out about 10 grid points along each boundary.

## What the conversion does

The CROCO history file must use the Vtransform 2 s-coordinate, store time in seconds since 2000-01-01 (the CROCO default), and hold snapshots regularly spaced from 00:00 of the first day to 00:00 after the last day.

### CROCO variables on the native grid

- land (`mask_rho == 0`, stored as 0 by CROCO) is set to NaN
- the depth of every s-level is computed from the Vtransform 2 equation, using the free surface of each snapshot
- values are linearly interpolated onto the 50 GLO12 depths: the top value is copied above the shallowest level,
  and values below the deepest level are NaN (no pit filling)
- `u` and `v` are averaged from cell faces to cell centres, keeping the zero velocity of land faces,
  then rotated by `angle` into eastward and northward components
- daily means use the trapezoidal rule over snapshots from 00:00 to 00:00 of the next day
- the outermost rows and columns are dropped
- each output variable keeps the floating point precision of the CROCO variable it comes from

### Horizontal regridding

The method follows the operational Mercator Ocean International regridder: SCRIP bilinear weights (Jones, 1999),
land corners dropped and the remaining weights renormalised.
The target grid covers the GLO12 points inside the CROCO latitude-longitude range.

- pyresample finds the four source points around each target point, on the sphere
- the fractional position inside that quadrilateral is solved by Newton iteration;
  the fractional distances of pyresample alone are off by up to one source cell when a target point lies
  on a source cell edge, for example a source column on a GLO12 meridian
- corners that are NaN (land, below the seabed, outside the domain) are dropped and the remaining weights
  renormalised, so a target point is NaN only when all four corners are
- target coordinates are computed in float32 as GLO12 stores them, `float32(first) + float32(k) * float32(1/12)`,
  and are bit-identical to the GLO12 coordinates, which OceanBench matches within 1e-4 degree

### Challenger format

The daily `time` axis of the forecast becomes `lead_day_index` 0, 1, 2, and so on, and its first day becomes `first_day_datetime`.

## Agulhas test case

The method was developed on a 5-day CROCO forecast of the Agulhas region (SEA-FORWARD, from 2026-10-21):
a curvilinear 159 by 99 grid of ca. 1/12 degree, rotated by up to 4 degrees, with 50 s-levels.

- a linear field of latitude and longitude is reproduced to within float32 precision on every target cell
- no regridded value leaves the range of the source values, and the domain-mean sea surface temperature changes
  by 0.02 °C at most
- no target point whose nearest CROCO point is ocean is left empty
- the RMSD against GLO12 over the Agulhas region above runs with 0.4 percent of ocean cells missing at most

The sponge layer width is estimated from the model output and still needs confirming against the model configuration.

## Not covered yet

- comparison against the operational regridder on the same input
- conservative remapping, needed when a challenger grid is finer than 1/12 degree
- filling coastal GLO12 ocean points that the challenger leaves empty (the drowning step of the operational regridder)
- processing a global 1/12 degree file in depth chunks to bound memory
